climate.overview_html: The dominant climate picture on September 6 is continuity: the Nepal–Tibet GLOF disaster holds at 1,318+ dead and 5,614+ missing with no material new toll figure overnight, while the WMO’s September 3 “off-the-charts” Super El Niño warning — near-100% probability of persistence through February 2027 — continues to set the baseline for every active hazard in this digest. Europe’s wildfire and drought emergency persists at 647,579 hectares burned (EFFIS data updated September 4) with very extreme fire danger forecast through September 9. The most vivid physical demonstration of Super El Niño’s energy remains the Pacific hurricane belt: Hurricane Lowell, which 30 hours ago was a Category 5 (160 mph), has weakened to Category 4 (130 mph) but now carries a Tropical Storm Watch for Kauai County and a Hurricane Watch for the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument as it approaches the Hawaiian Islands for a Monday close-pass.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse: STABLE — 1,318+ Dead (1,287 Nepal + 31 Tibet); 5,614+ Missing; Debris 240 km Inside India; Barrier Lake Risk Ongoing; 5,000+ Rescuers Active
items.summary: No material change in casualty figures reported on September 6: 1,287 confirmed dead in Nepal and 31 in Tibet, with 5,083 missing in Nepal and 531 missing in Tibet — a combined minimum of 1,318 dead and 5,614 missing, consistent with September 5 reporting. The disaster originated on August 27 from the collapse of a section of Langtang Lirung glacier at approximately 5,200 metres, generating a seismic signal of magnitude Ms 5.2 detected worldwide. Debris temporarily dammed the Lhende River before breaking, releasing a catastrophic flood down a 72 km corridor along the Trishuli River. Flood-borne debris has been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. Chinese authorities continue to warn that surrounding glaciers 'may still collapse, posing significant potential risks.' An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police remain on search operations. The event represents one of the deadliest glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) on instrumental record globally.

items.headline: WMO September 3 Warning: Super El Niño Could Be “Off the Charts” — Strongest Since Monitoring Began; Near-100% Probability El Niño Persists Through February 2027; 2027 on Track for Warmest Year on Record
items.summary: The World Meteorological Organization issued an unprecedented El Niño warning on September 3, stating the developing event could become the strongest since systematic monitoring began. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo: 'If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began — literally off the charts we have used for the past four decades.' WMO assigned nearly 100% probability — its highest-ever expressed certainty in an El Niño/La Niña advisory — that El Niño will persist through at least February 2027. Met Office head of long-range forecasting Adam Scaife: 'I have never seen an El Niño signal this intense in our forecasts.' Climate scientist Daniel Swain estimates ~70% probability this event will exceed the 2015–16 record on the multi-variate ENSO index. Because ocean heat releases into the atmosphere on a lagged timescale, peak atmospheric warming will arrive in 2027, raising the prospect of 2027 becoming the warmest year on record.

items.headline: EU Wildfires 2026: 647,579 Hectares Burned (EFFIS Updated September 4) — Very Extreme Fire Danger Through September 9 Across Iberia, France, Alps, Balkans, Greece, Turkey, Ukraine; Rhine Lowest Since 1880; Danube Record Low; Paks Nuclear Curtailed
items.summary: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area of 647,579 hectares as of the September 4 data update — a minor revision from the 647,375 ha figure in the September 3 reporting, consistent with ongoing fire activity. Very extreme fire danger is forecast through September 9 across a broad arc from Iberia and France through the Alps, western Balkans, northern Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. The strongest warm temperature anomaly covers southeastern Europe and the western Balkans. The 2026 season continues tracking ahead of the long-term average of 328,010 ha for the same date period (2006–2025), though below the record 2025 season tally (1,034,552 ha final). Rhine water levels remain at their lowest since 1880; the Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues curtailing output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances.

items.headline: Climate Change Is Now Europe’s Biggest Systemic Security Threat — 10,000 Excess Deaths From June Heatwave; 9M Tonnes Crop Loss; Military Assets Diverted to Fire Suppression and Flood Defense
items.summary: Chatham House published a policy analysis concluding that climate change is now Europe's biggest systemic security risk. The summer of 2026 provides the evidence base: extreme heat contributed to an estimated 10,000 excess deaths during the June heatwave alone and destroyed approximately 9 million tonnes of crops. The security dimension is direct: Europe's armed forces are increasingly deployed to fight fires, reinforce flood defenses, evacuate populations, and restore critical infrastructure — diverting capacity from conventional security operations. Rhine water levels fell to their lowest since 1880. Chatham House argues climate adaptation investment has structurally lagged behind mitigation spending and that European security planning must treat climate hazard as a primary threat category.

items.headline: NOAA August ENSO Diagnostic: Niño 3.4 Reaches +2.7°C Week of August 12; All 15 Ensemble Members Forecast Peak >+2.5°C; >90% Probability “Very Strong” Event Sept–Nov 2026; No La Niña Transition Before Spring 2027
items.summary: NOAA CPC's August 2026 ENSO Diagnostic confirms El Niño is tracking toward historically extreme territory. The Niño 3.4 index reached +2.7°C in the week centered on August 12 — already exceeding the +2.5°C 'very strong' threshold. All 15 coupled model ensemble members forecast Niño 3.4 exceeding +2.5°C at the September–November peak; a majority project exceedance of +3.0°C, which would qualify this event as a 'Super El Niño' comparable to 2015–16. NOAA assigns greater than 90% probability to a very strong event during September–November 2026 with little indication of a transition away from El Niño before spring 2027. The September 3 WMO update reinforced this with even higher certainty language.

major_events.name: Hurricane Lowell (Central Pacific) — STATUS CHANGE: Weakened to Category 4 (130 mph) From Cat 5; Tropical Storm Watch Kauai County & Niihau; Hurricane Watch Papahānaumokuākea (Nihoa to French Frigate Shoals); Center 630 mi SSW of Līhuʻe Saturday PM; North Turn Sunday; West of Kauai/Niihau Late Monday
major_events.status: CATEGORY 4 · 130 MPH · TSW KAUAI COUNTY · HW PAPAHANAUMOKUAKEA · NORTH TURN SUNDAY · KAUAI LATE MONDAY
major_events.impact: Hurricane Lowell weakened from Category 5 (160 mph) to Category 4 status with maximum sustained winds near 130 mph on Saturday September 6, as the storm lost some intensity after its historic rapid intensification. As of Saturday afternoon the center was located approximately 630 miles south-southwest of Līhuʻe, Kauai. A Tropical Storm Watch was issued for Kauai County, including Niihau — the first formal watch-level action for any inhabited Hawaiian island during this event. A Hurricane Watch was simultaneously issued for the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument from Nihoa to French Frigate Shoals. The storm is forecast to continue drifting west-northwest through Saturday night before a sharp turn to the north on Sunday under a weakening mid-level ridge, bringing the center to the vicinity of Kauai and Niihau late Monday and Monday night. Kauai can expect 4 to 8 inches of rainfall with maximum isolated totals exceeding 12 inches; the Big Island 2 to 6 inches with isolated 10 inches. Tropical storm conditions (sustained winds of at least 39 mph) are expected for Kauai County by late Monday or Monday night. Dangerous surf and rip currents already affect all island shores. Hawaii remains under a statewide emergency declaration.

major_events.name: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods — ONGOING: 1,318+ Dead; 5,614+ Missing; Barrier Lake Risk; 5,000+ Rescuers
major_events.status: 1,318+ DEAD · 5,614+ MISSING · BARRIER LAKE RISK · RESCUE ONGOING · NO MATERIAL TOLL CHANGE
major_events.impact: The combined death toll from the August 27 Nepal-Tibet glacier collapse holds at 1,287 confirmed dead in Nepal plus 31 in Tibet, with 5,083 missing in Nepal and 531 missing in Tibet. No material new toll figure was reported September 6. Flood debris has been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. Chinese authorities continue to warn that surrounding glaciers 'may still collapse.' An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police continue search operations.

major_events.name: Malaysia / SE Asia Wildfire Haze — STATUS CHANGE: 1.4 Million Students Now Attending Remotely; Haze Spreads to Philippines; Serian Emergency Ongoing; Singapore Air Quality Improving
major_events.status: SERIAN EMERGENCY ONGOING · 1.4M STUDENTS REMOTE · PHILIPPINES IMPACT · CLOUD-SEEDING CONTINUING
major_events.impact: The regional haze emergency escalated Saturday with an estimated 1.4 million students across Malaysia attending school remotely as hazardous air quality persists across much of Sarawak, peninsular Malaysia, and now extends to the Philippines. Malaysia's formal emergency in the Serian Division, Sarawak (API peaked at 521 on September 4) remains in effect. Cloud-seeding operations continue. The haze from Indonesian peat and forest fires in Kalimantan has now reached the Philippines and Brunei in addition to Singapore and Malaysia. Indonesia's Forestry Ministry reported 717 fire hot spots nationally since August 1. El Niño-driven dry conditions are forecast to sustain elevated fire risk through early October.

major_events.name: Hurricane Marie (Eastern Pacific) — ONGOING: Category 2 (100 mph); No Landfall Forecast
major_events.impact: Hurricane Marie continues as a Category 2 storm with maximum sustained winds near 100 mph off the Mexican coast, tracking west-northwestward into the open eastern Pacific. No landfall is forecast. The storm continues to be supported by the above-normal sea surface temperatures sustained by Super El Niño thermodynamics.

major_events.name: Hurricane Karina (Eastern Pacific) — Becoming Post-Tropical; No Hawaii Threat; Dissipating
major_events.status: BECOMING POST-TROPICAL · DISSIPATING · NO HAWAII THREAT
major_events.impact: Hurricane Karina continues on its forecast dissipation track, expected to become post-tropical by Monday before dissipating entirely in hostile conditions — drier air intrusion, lower sea surface temperatures, and increasing vertical wind shear. No threat to Hawaii or any other land area.

major_events.name: Europe Wildfire and Drought Emergency — ONGOING: 647,579 ha Burned; Very Extreme Fire Danger Through September 9; Rhine Lowest Since 1880; Paks Nuclear Curtailed
major_events.status: ONGOING · 647,579 HA · VERY EXTREME FIRE DANGER THROUGH SEPT 9 · RHINE LOWEST SINCE 1880
major_events.impact: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area at 647,579 hectares as of the September 4 data refresh, a marginal increase. Very extreme fire danger continues through September 9 across Iberia, France, the Alps, western Balkans, northern Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. The atmospheric blocking pattern has strengthened rather than broken. Rhine water levels remain at their lowest since 1880; the Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues to curtail output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances.

major_events.name: Pakistan Monsoon Flooding — ONGOING: 299+ Dead; Peak Season; 2–3 More September Pulse Events Forecast
major_events.status: ONGOING · 299+ DEAD · PEAK MONSOON · 2–3 MORE SEPTEMBER SPELLS FORECAST
major_events.impact: Pakistan's cumulative monsoon season death toll stands at 299 (including 140 children) per the most recent NDMA reporting. This year's rainfall is running 50–60% heavier than the comparable period last year. NDMA continues to forecast 2–3 additional monsoon pulse events during September — the season's climatological peak.

major_events.name: BC Bald Range Wildfire — HELD: ~25,163 Hectares; Phased Re-Entry Ongoing; Summerland Partial Orders Active
major_events.status: HELD · ~25,163 HA · PHASED RE-ENTRY · SUMMERLAND PARTIAL ORDERS
major_events.impact: The Bald Range wildfire near Summerland maintains its HELD classification with no material change in fire extent (~25,163 ha). The Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen EOC is conducting phased re-entry planning; pre-conditions including utilities, roads, and safety checks must be met before broader re-entry. Peachland and Electoral Area West properties are under an Evacuation Alert. Some portions of Summerland remain under Evacuation Orders. Temporary Access Permits continue to be issued case-by-case.

weather.overview_html: The key development on September 6 is Hurricane Lowell’s weakening from Category 5 (160 mph) to Category 4 (130 mph), even as the first formal watches were issued: a Tropical Storm Watch for Kauai County (including Niihau) and a Hurricane Watch for the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument from Nihoa to French Frigate Shoals. The center was located 630 miles south-southwest of Līhuʻe Saturday afternoon, forecast to pass west of Kauai and Niihau late Monday and Monday night, bringing 4–8 inches of rain to Kauai (locally exceeding 12 inches) and dangerous surf already affecting all island shores. In Southeast Asia, the Indonesia-driven haze emergency has expanded to an estimated 1.4 million students attending school remotely, with the smoke plume now reaching the Philippines. The Nepal–Tibet GLOF toll holds at 1,318+ dead and 5,614+ missing with no material overnight change.

items.headline: Hurricane Lowell Weakens to Category 4 (130 mph); Tropical Storm Watch Kauai County; Hurricane Watch Papahānaumokuākea; 630 mi SSW of Līhuʻe Saturday PM; West of Kauai/Niihau Late Monday; 4–8” Rain Kauai; Statewide Emergency Active
items.summary: Hurricane Lowell weakened from Category 5 (160 mph) to Category 4 with maximum sustained winds near 130 mph by Saturday September 6, losing some of the intensity it had achieved during its remarkable 30-hour rapid intensification from tropical storm to Category 5. As of Saturday afternoon the center was approximately 630 miles south-southwest of Līhuʻe. A Tropical Storm Watch was issued for Kauai County including Niihau; a Hurricane Watch was issued for the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument from Nihoa to French Frigate Shoals. The storm is forecast to continue drifting westward through Saturday before turning sharply northward on Sunday, passing west of Kauai and Niihau late Monday and Monday night at still-major-hurricane strength with gradual weakening. Kauai can expect 4–8 inches of rainfall with maximum isolated totals exceeding 12 inches and the potential for flash flooding and mudslides in steep terrain. Tropical storm conditions (39+ mph sustained winds) are expected for Kauai County by late Monday or Monday night. Dangerous surf and rip currents already impact all island shores. Hawaii remains under a Governor-declared statewide emergency.

items.summary: The confirmed death toll from the August 27 Nepal-Tibet glacier collapse stands at 1,287 dead in Nepal and 31 in Tibet, with 5,083 missing in Nepal and 531 missing in Tibet, for a combined total of at least 1,318 dead and 5,614 missing as of September 5 reporting. The disaster originated from a glacier collapse on Langtang Lirung at approximately 5,200 metres elevation, generating a seismic signal of Ms 5.2. items.headline: Hurricane Marie: Category 2 (100 mph); No Landfall Forecast; El Niño SSTs Supporting Eastern Pacific Activity
items.summary: Hurricane Marie continues as a Category 2 storm with maximum sustained winds near 100 mph, tracking west-northwestward into the open eastern Pacific. No landfall is forecast. The above-normal sea surface temperatures sustained by Super El Niño thermodynamics continue to support tropical cyclone development across the eastern and central Pacific during the peak of the hurricane season.

renewables.overview_html: No major new project or deal announcements emerged on September 6 in the renewables sector. The week’s leading milestone remains the September 1 installation of the first of 53 monopiles at OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII), RWE and TotalEnergies’ 795 MW North Sea project using Vestas V236-15 MW turbines, scheduled to supply ~1 million Dutch households by early 2028. In the US structural story, EIA data confirm solar, wind and storage added 44,889 MW in the year to June 2026 versus only 7,530 MW for natural gas, with combined renewable installed capacity on pace to surpass the entire gas fleet within approximately 12 months — a milestone underscored by the IEA’s confirmation that global renewable generation has overtaken coal-fired output in 2026 for the first time, with renewables making up 36% of global power supply against coal’s 32%. The federal–state collision continues: California’s lawsuit over the Trump administration’s $120 million buyout of the 2 GW Golden State Wind lease proceeds. UK plug-in solar remains a live consumer market after SI 2026/848 legalised 800 W residential socket systems from August 27, now available at 800+ Argos stores.

items.headline: OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) First Monopile Installed — 795 MW RWE/TotalEnergies JV; 53 Vestas V236-15 MW Turbines; 53 km Off Dutch Coast; 1 Million Dutch Households by 2028; Transition-Piece-Less Design
items.summary: The offshore installation vessel Les Alizés successfully installed the first of 53 monopiles for OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) on September 1, 53 km west of IJmuiden in the Dutch North Sea. The 795 MW project is a joint venture between RWE and TotalEnergies, using 53 Vestas V236-15 MW turbines — among the largest offshore turbines commercially deployed. The project uses innovative transition-piece-less monopiles, where turbine towers bolt directly to the monopile without a transition piece, reducing steel per foundation. Installation of all 53 monopiles is expected to complete by early 2027; turbine installation in 2027; fully operational by early 2028, supplying approximately 1 million Dutch households.

items.headline: EIA Data: US Renewables Installed Capacity to Surpass Natural Gas Within 12 Months — Solar+Wind Added 44,889 MW vs. Gas’s 7,530 MW in Year to June 2026; Battery Storage Up 17,859 MW
items.summary: New EIA capacity data show US renewable energy installed capacity is on pace to surpass natural gas within approximately 12 months — most likely by summer 2027. In the year through June 30, 2026: utility-scale solar added 28,077 MW; small-scale solar 6,492 MW; wind 10,553 MW; combined renewables 44,889 MW. Natural gas capacity grew only 7,530 MW in the same period. Battery storage added 17,859 MW. When combined renewables capacity eventually exceeds natural gas's installed base, it will mark a structural inflection in the US power system. Separately, IEA data confirm US wind and solar output climbed 10% in H1 2026, reaching 20% of the grid mix and surpassing coal and nuclear generation for the first time.

items.headline: California Sues Trump Administration Over $120 Million Deal to Cancel 2 GW Golden State Wind Offshore Lease; Alleges Violations of Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act; $100M in Port/Transmission Prep Already Spent
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta and the California Energy Commission filed suit August 28 challenging the Interior Department's agreement to pay $120 million to abandon the 2 GW Golden State Wind offshore lease and invest instead in fossil fuel projects. The complaint alleges violations of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, the Judgment Fund Act, and other federal statutes. The 2 GW project would have supplied clean electricity to more than 1 million California homes. California notes it has already spent more than $100 million on port upgrades, transmission improvements, and other infrastructure in preparation for the project.

items.headline: UK Plug-In Solar Panels Legal Across Great Britain From August 27 — SI 2026/848 Enables 800 W Residential Systems Via Standard Sockets; Available at 800+ Argos Stores; Saves Up to £110/Year
items.summary: Plug-in solar panels became legal for residential use across England, Wales, and Scotland from August 27, 2026, under Plug-In Solar Amendment SI 2026/848. The regulation allows compliant systems with a maximum rated AC output of 800 W to connect via a standard plug without planning permission or a certified electrician — creating a legal pathway similar to Germany, France, and the Netherlands. Systems are immediately available at over 800 Argos stores and are estimated to save households up to £110 per year.

science.overview_html: Three new papers this week deepen the tropical cyclone forecasting frontier directly relevant to Hurricane Lowell’s Monday approach to Kauai: arXiv:2609.02085 (TC-Next) demonstrates zero-shot transfer of a multimodal foundation-model-based TC tracker trained only on GraphCast/Western Pacific data, cutting track error 15–44% and intensity error 3–6× versus conventional trackers when applied without retraining to Pangu-Weather and IFS HRES forecast fields; arXiv:2609.03364 evaluates the added value of dynamical downscaling for sub-seasonal tropical cyclone prediction using KMA’s GloSea6, finding significant intensity and track underestimation especially in August; and the earlier arXiv:2609.03210 IMERG fine-tuning paper achieves up to 19% CRPS improvement and a 57% Brier skill score gain for extreme rainfall over NWP. The broader ML sub-seasonal competition landscape gained a spotlight via the ECMWF AI Weather Quest science blog previewing the September 24 annual awards ceremony: DJF 2025/26 winner is MicroEnsemble, a Microsoft-led team that AI-post-processes ECMWF dynamical output. The dominant story from earlier this week, Google DeepMind’s WeatherNext 3 — first global AI model on raw observations and live geostationary satellite data, 5-km hourly surface resolution, tops Brightband WeatherBench, live in Google Search/Gemini/Maps, remains the headline model release of the period.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03582 (WeatherNext 3): Google DeepMind’s Hourly 5-km Global AI Weather Model Trains on Raw Observations; 60% Better Precipitation vs. WN2; 100-m Wind-Height Forecasts; Tops Brightband WeatherBench; Live in Google Search, Gemini, Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind & Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 · September 3, 2026 · Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, BigQuery, Earth Engine
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 is the first major global AI model to ingest live geostationary satellite data directly and train on raw weather station observations — eliminating the 6-to-7-hour data lag of NWP-based AI models and shrinking it to 3–4 hours with hourly forecast cycles. Resolution: 5 km for key surface variables, 10 km for other surface variables, 25 km for atmospheric variables, and explicit 100-meter hub-height wind forecasts for wind turbine applications alongside cloud cover and solar radiation for grid operators. WeatherNext 3 has 2.4× more parameters than WeatherNext 2. Precipitation evaluation shows CRPS improvements of up to 60% against IMERG and 50% Brier score reduction versus NWP baselines at early lead times. On Brightband's Operational WeatherBench, WeatherNext 3 ranks first across temperature, wind speed, and humidity. Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps, BigQuery, and Google Earth Engine.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03364: Added Value of Dynamical Downscaling in Sub-Seasonal Tropical Cyclone Forecast — GloSea6 Underestimates TC Frequency, Tracks, Lifetime, and Intensity; Largest Errors in August; Downscaling Partially Corrects Bias
items.meta: Kim et al. (Korea Meteorological Administration) · arXiv:2609.03364 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: This study evaluates the characteristics of tropical cyclones in sub-seasonal forecasts using GloSea6, the operational seasonal-to-sub-seasonal forecasting model of the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA), over the western North Pacific during JJAS 1993–2016. GloSea6 is found to underestimate TC frequency, tracks (particularly in mid-latitudes), lifetime, and intensity across all months, with the most significant errors occurring in August — precisely the period of highest climatological TC activity. The paper evaluates whether dynamical downscaling to higher resolution can recover the lost skill for track and intensity. The results are directly relevant to the current Super El Niño season, during which TC forecast accuracy is critical for Hawaii (Lowell), the Philippines, and Japan.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03210: Fine-Tuning AI Weather Model With IMERG Precipitation Observations Improves Medium-Range CRPS by Up to 19% and Extreme Rainfall Brier Skill by 57%; Tropical Storms and Drizzle Also Improved
items.meta: Schmitt, Delorme, King, Patodia, Schneider, Sheshadri, Jain · arXiv:2609.03210 · September 2, 2026
items.summary: Artificial intelligence weather prediction (AIWP) systems now surpass state-of-the-art physical models for medium-range forecasting, but current global AIWP models are trained almost exclusively on the ERA5 reanalysis, which has known biases particularly for precipitation. This paper fine-tunes a graph-transformer AIWP architecture directly with IMERG precipitation observational data at 0.25° resolution. Results: medium-range continuous ranked probability scores (CRPS) improve by up to 19%; Brier skill score for extreme rainfall prediction improves by 57% globally over state-of-the-art operational NWP models. The fine-tuned model also demonstrates superior skill for tropical storm precipitation and drizzle events. The approach is directly relevant to the acute precipitation hazards active in this digest: Hurricane Lowell threatening Hawaii, Pakistan's monsoon, and Nepal's ongoing flood response.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.02085 (TC-Next): Zero-Shot Multimodal Cyclone Forecasting — Trained Only on GraphCast/Western Pacific; Cuts Track Error 15–44% and Intensity Error 3–6× vs. Conventional Trackers; Transfers Without Retraining to Pangu-Weather and IFS HRES
items.meta: Wang, Chen, Luo, Kim, Chang · arXiv:2609.02085 · September 2, 2026
items.summary: TC-Next is a multimodal deep learning model that forecasts tropical cyclone track and intensity at 6–24 h lead times by jointly leveraging a foundation model's atmospheric forecast fields (kinematic and thermodynamic) and GridSat infrared satellite imagery. Trained exclusively on GraphCast forecast fields over the Western Pacific, TC-Next lowers track error by 15–44% and intensity error by a factor of 3–6 relative to the conventional rule-based tracker TempestExtremes. Critically, when applied zero-shot — without retraining — to forecast fields from Pangu-Weather and IFS HRES, TC-Next remains substantially ahead of TempestExtremes on both track and intensity, demonstrating strong model-agnostic generalization. The result suggests that multimodal satellite-plus-NWP architectures can provide superior TC guidance across the full spectrum of operational forecast systems, including AI-based ones.

items.headline: ECMWF AI Weather Quest: First Year Concludes — 42 Teams From 30+ Countries Submitted Sub-Seasonal Forecasts; DJF 2025/26 Winner MicroEnsemble (Microsoft-Led) Post-Processes ECMWF Dynamics With AI; Annual Awards Ceremony September 24
items.meta: ECMWF Science Blog · September 2026 · Competition phase: August 2025–September 2026 · Annual awards: 24 Sep 2026
items.summary: ECMWF's AI Weather Quest — an international competition for AI/ML sub-seasonal forecasting operating from August 2025 to September 2026 — is now concluding its first year, with an annual highlights and awards ceremony scheduled for September 24. The competition required participants to submit real-time global sub-seasonal forecasts at 1.5° resolution, providing quintile probabilities for weekly-mean temperature, precipitation, and sea level pressure for the Days 19–25 and Days 26–32 windows. Across the full year, 42 teams from countries including the US, China, and diverse nations across Africa, Latin America, and Asia submitted at least one forecast, with weekly participation never dropping below 25 teams. The DJF 2025/26 period winner was MicroEnsemble, a Microsoft-led team comprising scientists with strengths in meteorology, engineering, statistics, and AI, whose approach uses AI to post-process state-of-the-art dynamical ECMWF forecasts — representing a hybrid AI-physical approach rather than a purely data-driven architecture. ECMWF's own AIFS-SUBS submission showed skill comparable to the IFS while using approximately 200× less energy at inference, extending skilful MJO forecasts by 8 days.

items.source: arXiv / Barcelona Supercomputing Center / ECML PKDD 2026
items.headline: arXiv 2609.00847: First Comprehensive Checklist for Energy and Carbon Footprints of ML/AI in Earth System Modeling; Barcelona Supercomputing Center; Presented at GREEN-AI Workshop, ECML PKDD 2026 Naples
items.meta: Dainelli, Mozaffari, Castaño et al. (BSC Earth Dept.) · arXiv:2609.00847 · September 1, 2026 · GREEN-AI Workshop, ECML PKDD 2026, Naples
items.summary: As machine learning finds its way into nearly every aspect of Earth system modeling, this Barcelona Supercomputing Center paper provides the first comprehensive checklist for ML/AI practitioners to assess and reduce the environmental footprint of their applications. The checklist is organized around successive pipeline stages — data curation, model architecture, training regime, inference, and deployment — with curated metrics for estimating energy consumption and carbon footprint at each stage. The work is timely given the explosive growth of compute-intensive neural weather models such as WeatherNext 3, GraphCast, and AIFS, and raises the question of whether the carbon cost of training and running these models is systematically accounted for. Presented at the GREEN-AI workshop of ECML PKDD 2026 in Naples.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.30795: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End AI Weather Forecasting — Aardvark Weather Made Probabilistic; Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty Decomposed; Probabilistic Fine-Tuning Improves Mean Forecast 4.2%
items.meta: Almeida, Otero, Arndt, Baur, Samek, Ma · arXiv:2608.30795 · Submitted 31 Aug 2026
items.summary: This paper renders the Aardvark Weather end-to-end AI weather system probabilistic by attaching two stochastic mechanisms: (1) learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder capturing aleatoric uncertainty; (2) Monte Carlo dropout in the processor capturing epistemic uncertainty. A law-of-total-variance decomposition attributes forecast spread to each source. Key result: probabilistic fine-tuning improves the mean forecast by 4.2% on average across variables and lead times — demonstrating that uncertainty decomposition and mean-forecast skill are mutually reinforcing rather than in tension.

items.headline: GRL: 245 Glacial Earthquakes Detected at Thwaites “Doomsday Glacier” Marine Edge 2010–2023 — Busiest Cluster 2018–2020 Coincided With Episodic Glacier Acceleration
items.meta: Pham et al. (Australian National University) · Geophysical Research Letters · Published 29 Aug 2026
items.summary: A study in Geophysical Research Letters presents the first systematic detection of 245 previously uncatalogued seismic events near Thwaites Glacier's marine edge, catalogued over 2010–2023. Most are likely glacial earthquakes caused by capsizing, calving icebergs colliding with the parent glacier. The 2018–2020 cluster was the busiest, coinciding with episodic acceleration of Thwaites' floating ice tongue toward the sea. The findings add seismic evidence to the broad body of research showing Thwaites' marine-based instability is accelerating — directly relevant as the Nepal–Tibet GLOF disaster underscores the expanding global glacial hazard under anthropogenic warming.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.26822 (Nested-EAGLE): Single ML System Bridges 0.25° Global and 6-km Regional Forecasting Over CONUS; Lower MSE Than Both GFS and HRRR for Near-Surface Fields
items.summary: A NOAA team introduces Nested-EAGLE, an ML weather prediction system that unifies short-range and medium-range forecasting in a single architecture — combining a 0.25° global model with a 6 km refinement over CONUS. Nested-EAGLE achieves significantly lower mean-squared error in near-surface and low-level quantities over CONUS compared to both GFS and HRRR, while remaining competitive globally. The unified short-and-medium-range system provides an improved distillation of global weather to local impacts from a single model.

items.headline: ECMWF Operationally Deploys AIFL: LSTM Global Streamflow Model Trained on 18,588 Basins; Detects 20-Year Flood Signal 6 Days in Advance; Enters Copernicus EMS Flood Service
items.summary: ECMWF's operationally deployed AIFL (AI for Floods) LSTM, trained on 18,588 river basins from the CARAVAN dataset, detects a 20-year return-level flood signal six days in advance — demonstrated during Storm Henk (Belgium, January 2024). The deployment within Copernicus Emergency Management Service provides global flood early warning directly relevant to the current extreme precipitation events in Pakistan, Nepal, and Southeast Asia.

items.title: Cyclic Materials Closes $75 Million Series C Led by T. Rowe Price to Scale US Rare Earth Recycling — Total Equity Now $237 Million; Arizona Facility Operational Q3 2026; South Carolina Campus Breaking Ground Q4; Critical Supply for Wind Turbines and EV Magnets
items.body_html: Cyclic Materials, a Canadian rare earth recycling company, closed a $75 million Series C financing round announced September 2, 2026, led by accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, bringing total equity funding to $237 million. Strategic investor ERI joined the round alongside existing backers Microsoft, Amazon, and others. Cyclic’s Hub-and-Spoke system recovers rare earth materials from permanent magnets in end-of-life wind turbines, EV motors, and manufacturing scrap, converting them into high-purity rare earth oxides — directly reducing Western dependence on Chinese primary rare earth supply. An Arizona magnet separation and critical mineral recycling plant is expected to begin operations during Q3 2026, with a South Carolina integrated rare earth recycling campus breaking ground in Q4 2026.
items.source_html: Cyclic Materials / Metal Tech News

items.title: Artemis London 2026: Cat Bond and ILS Market Well-Positioned for Disciplined Growth; AFME Calls for ILS to Back Climate Policies; 220 Attendees, 120+ Organizations; London Bridge Cat Bonds and LoC Capital Stacks Discussed
items.body_html: The Artemis London 2026 conference on September 1 convened approximately 220 attendees from more than 120 organizations across the ILS ecosystem, including specialists, (re)insurance buyers, investors, fund managers, and service providers. Speakers highlighted discipline in the catastrophe bond market and expected continued growth. The Association for Financial Markets in Europe (AFME) called for ILS and catastrophe bonds as effective mechanisms for insurers to access new capital to back climate-related policies — directly relevant as the Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report, released the same day, put average annual insured losses at a record $171 billion. The convergence of ILS market growth, the Verisk benchmark revision, Hurricane Lowell’s Hawaii threat, and the Nepal–Tibet disaster illustrates the direct line from extreme weather under Super El Niño to capital markets.

items.title: Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report: Industry Should Prepare for $171 Billion Average Annual Insured Losses — Up $19 Billion Year-on-Year; US Accounts for $117B (68%); 100-Year Loss at $477B; Highest Estimate Verisk Has Ever Reported
items.body_html: Verisk released its 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report on September 1, calculating that the insurance industry should be prepared to absorb $171 billion in insured catastrophe losses on an average annual basis — up $19 billion from the prior-year estimate and the highest average annual loss figure Verisk has ever published. Of the $171 billion global insured AAL, $117 billion (68%) is attributed to the United States; the 100-year return-period scenario yields $477 billion in aggregate insured losses, and the 250-year scenario reaches $606 billion. A companion release covers Europe: Europe carries $110 billion in expected annual economic catastrophe losses, of which only about $24 billion is currently insured — a protection gap of roughly 78%. Severe thunderstorm accounts for 40% of modelled risk, followed by tropical cyclone (27%), earthquake (10%), winter storm (9%), flood (7%), and wildfire (6%).
items.source_html: GlobeNewswire / Verisk / Insurance Journal

items.title: Redstone Closes €25 Million First Tranche of Blue Economy Decarbonization Fund — Targeting Maritime Carbon Reduction, Ocean Asset Security, and Coastal Infrastructure Resilience
items.body_html: Berlin- and Helsinki-based fund manager Redstone closed the first tranche of its blue economy decarbonization fund at €25 million during the week of August 28, targeting investments in technologies to decarbonize maritime sectors, secure ocean-based assets, and build resilient coastal infrastructure. The fund addresses a sector responsible for approximately 2.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Alternative fuels (ammonia, methanol, green hydrogen), hull efficiency technologies, and port electrification represent core investment themes. The first close reflects growing investor interest in maritime decarbonization as the IMO’s strengthened 2050 net-zero shipping target creates regulatory pull.

items.title: BlocPower Shuts Down and Liquidates — Community Clean Energy Electrification Platform Winds Down After 14 Years; Returns Capital to Investors
items.body_html: BlocPower, the community-focused clean energy company that electrified buildings in low-income urban neighborhoods by replacing gas heating with heat pumps and solar, is shutting down and liquidating its assets, returning remaining capital to investors. BlocPower had operated since 2012, achieving significant attention for decarbonizing community buildings in underserved neighborhoods across New York City and other markets. The closure is a notable setback for impact-oriented community climate tech and underscores the structural challenges facing mission-driven platforms trying to deploy clean energy in underserved markets at scale.
